### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2b22846f5bad2b2017906cfd80aa86c22ac2d24f` — the merge of head `920db11e64204a453a7ed6d479ced57caaa4d506` into base `493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2b22846f5bad2b2017906cfd80aa86c22ac2d24f && git checkout 2b22846f5bad2b2017906cfd80aa86c22ac2d24f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3 920db11e64204a453a7ed6d479ced57caaa4d506 && git checkout -B drift-repro 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3 && git merge --no-ff 920db11e64204a453a7ed6d479ced57caaa4d506

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a)

## 维护者速读
这个 PR 做的是：有人在一串评论里回复时，通知这一串的发起人，以及之前在这一串里回复过的人。卡上的几条规则都做到了：
- 回复的人自己不收通知。
- 这条回复里已经被「提到」的人只收提到的那一条通知，不会再收一条。
- 看不到这条记录或这条回复的人，不收通知。判断用的是和「提到」完全同一道权限检查。

通知的样子、语言、邮件每人每 10 分钟最多一封，都和「提到」一致。「提到」原来的通知完全没动。

判断「参与过的人」的方式在正文里写清楚了：顺着回复往上找到这一串的第一条评论，再用一条分组查询找出所有回复过的人，不把整串评论读进内存。

没有需要修的问题。下面两条小建议不挡合并：
- 找「这一串的人」时，建议再核对一下上级评论确实属于同一条记录。
- 一串里人很多时，每发一条回复要逐个判断并发通知，会让发评论这一步变慢，可以以后观察。

不属于受管面，声明了对外新增（新通知类型和三个文案），所以座位还要在同一版本上跑一次 L2，本记录不替代它。

**Head reviewed:** `c83ad1dc3704566bbc09d6b02a62b947e40f3ed2`. Three commits, 11 files, +779/−33. `git merge-tree` onto current `main` is clean. `check-governed-merges --pr 36098` (PR-head register) reads **NOT governed**, 0 of 11 paths, 812 lines, under the 3000-line threshold. `reviewFace` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` gives face `declaration` → `TIER_DEFAULT`, so the seat's declaration L2 on this head is the review that face owes. CI is as the thread reported. vitest was not run here (no `node_modules`).

### What holds
- **Candidates vs recipients.**
  - `readThreadParticipants` reads in system context, and only to produce candidates. Every candidate then goes through `admitMentionRecipients`, the same gate a mention uses, judged in the candidate's own envelope.
  - Record read comes first, then the comment read gate on this reply's id (`readableIn(… COMMENT_OBJECT, commentId)`), then the organisation claim.
  - `notice: 'reply'` only changes the log line; the verdict is untouched.
  - The author is never handed the reply's withheld set, and `onMentionsWithheld` still names only mentioned users, so nothing about un-named people reaches the author. The `data-engine.mdx` paragraph states this.
- **Skips.**
  - The author is removed before the gate, and again in the emit loop.
  - `named` collects the mentions as entered and both halves of the gate's answer (`userIds` and `withheld`), so a mentioned user never gets a second notice. A withheld mention would fail the same gate here anyway.
  - `writeCommentNotices` runs the mention writer first, and it is the only `afterInsert` registration on `sys_comment`. `afterUpdate` keeps `writeCommentMentions` alone, so an edit notifies no participant.
- **SQL first.**
  - The ancestry walk reads one row per hop, bounded at 16 and cycle-safe.
  - Repliers come from one `aggregate(… { where: { parent_id }, groupBy: ['author_id'] })` on the `parent_id` index (`sys-comment.object.ts:315`). No thread rows are materialised.
  - A missing parent returns `null`, which means no notice.
- **Topic and e-mail.**
  - `collab.reply` goes through the same `messaging.emit` ingress.
  - The inbox `dedupKey` is per reply and person.
  - `replyEmailDedupKey` shares the mention's 10-minute bucket under its own prefix, and `mentionEmailDedupKey` is byte-identical to before (`commentEmailDedupKey(MENTION_TOPIC, …)`).
  - `REPLY_EMAIL_TEMPLATES` is the same generator under the reply topic, registered in its own `try`.
  - None of the new constants is exported from `index.ts`.
- **Strings.** There are three keys in all eleven locales of `translations/messages.ts`, with English fallbacks inline.
- **Clause-② `yes (widening)` is right.** A new emitted topic and new host i18n keys are added, and nothing is removed or refused. `patch` matches the precedent the body cites.
- **Acceptance coverage.** Each of the card's six acceptance lines maps to a named case in `comment-reply-notice.integration.test.ts` (real ObjectQL over SQLite, real messaging pipeline) or `mention-recipient-gate.integration.test.ts` (starter who lost record read). The body explains how participants are found, which is the sixth line.

### Nits (do not block)
- **N1: the parent chain is not held to the reply's own thread.** `readThreadParticipants` follows `parent_id` and groups on `parent_id = root` without comparing `thread_id`, and nothing on insert checks that a reply's parent hangs off the same record (`comment-access-hooks.ts` authorises `thread_id` only).
  - Through the Console the two always agree. A reply written through the API with a parent from another record would draw its candidates from that other thread.
  - Every candidate still has to read *this* record and *this* reply, so no notice goes to someone who cannot see it.
  - The cheap hardening is to read `thread_id` on each hop, stop when it differs from the reply's, and add `thread_id` to the aggregate's `where`. "The thread" then means this record's thread by construction.
- **N2: fan-out cost grows with the thread.**
  - Per candidate, the gate resolves the user, builds their context and runs two read checks. The writer then resolves a locale and makes two emits, all sequentially inside the reply's `afterInsert`.
  - Mentions were bounded by what an author types, while a reply's fan-out is bounded by how many people have replied.
  - That is fine for phase 1. If long threads appear, a cap, or moving the reply notice after the write's response, is the lever.

### Observation (no change asked)
- In a deeper chain, which the Console does not write, the author of the comment directly replied to is not the starter, so they get "replied in a comment thread you are in" rather than "replied to your comment". The body already states that the Console writes one level.

### Landing terms
- Not governed. After the seat's declaration L2 on this head, it lands through the ordinary queue. `Fixes #36074` closes the card on merge.
- A new push needs a delta L1 unless it is a clean main merge.
- This review does not approve, mark ready, enqueue or request review.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c83ad1dc3704566bbc09d6b02a62b947e40f3ed2`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #36074 (body, triage 7062833356, claim 7063189874, amendment 7063394639); epic #36062 body with 7062530606 and 7062566069; sibling #36071 body; PR body, file list (11 files) and the net diff against merge-base `493ad095d4`; the check-runs on the head. Every check-run on the head is `success` or `skipped`, except one `cancelled` run of PR-body guards whose rerun on the same head is `success`. Gate families are taken as answered.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **New notification topic `collab.reply`** (inbox and e-mail, through `messaging.emit`). Named right as a widening: a new value in `sys_notification.topic` and `sys_inbox_message.topic`, plus a new `messaging.registerBuiltinTemplates` set (`REPLY_EMAIL_TEMPLATES`, one per catalog locale), registered by its own call at `kernel:ready`.
2. **Three new `messages.*` keys** (`repliedToYourComment`, `repliedInYourThread`, `repliedAnonymous`), present in all 11 locales of `translations/messages.ts`. Named right as a widening. The `#36070` precedent applies.
3. **`MentionGateInput.notice?: 'mention' | 'reply'`**. Optional, and it changes only the log line. `mention-recipient-gate.ts` is not exported from `index.ts`, so the change is internal. With the field absent, the line reads exactly as before. Named right: no surface change.
4. **`mention-email.ts`**. `REPLY_TOPIC`, `replyEmailDedupKey` and `REPLY_EMAIL_TEMPLATES` are package-internal. `mentionEmailDedupKey` and `MENTION_EMAIL_TEMPLATES` are byte-identical in output, because the refactor goes through `commentEmailDedupKey` and `commentEmailTemplates` with the same shape. Named right.
5. **`writeCommentMentions` now returns `ReadonlySet`**. It is still registered on `afterUpdate`. The engine's `triggerHooks` ignores handler return values (`engine-hooks-and-functions.ts`), so the edit path is unchanged. Named right.
6. **The accept set is unchanged.** No spec, protocol, REST or SDK shape moves, and no `sys_comment` field or permission changes. Named right.
7. ⛔ **Named wrong: the platform topic list served by the preference-options door.** `packages/services/service-messaging/src/preference-options.ts` `PLATFORM_NOTIFICATION_TOPICS` is the platform's measured list of fixed topics. It is served as the `platform` source of `GET /api/v1/messaging/preference-options`, which feeds the `notification-topic` widget on `sys_notification_preference.topic` and on the template `topic`. Its jsdoc states the rule: "a feature that starts sending a new fixed topic adds it here". `#35789` followed that rule for `messaging.slack_link_removed`. This diff starts sending a new fixed platform topic but does not add `collab.reply` to the list. The PR body's Clause-② re-read justifies that with "no topic registry exists". That holds for ADR-0030's `defineTopic()` catalog, but it is wrong for the list this door serves.
   - Effect: the changeset's own **Preferences** bullet tells an administrator to write a `(collab.reply, email, enabled: false)` row. In an organization that has no stored reply notice yet, the console's topic picker does not offer `collab.reply`, and the template picker does not offer it either. The topic is still legal as free text, so nothing is refused.
   - **Required fix:**
     - add `'collab.reply'` to `PLATFORM_NOTIFICATION_TOPICS`, kept sorted, right after `'collab.mention'`;
     - name it in that jsdoc's `plugin-audit` parenthesis;
     - add an `'@objectstack/service-messaging': patch` entry to the changeset, with a bullet that says the preference and template topic list now offers `collab.reply`;
     - correct the PR body sentence.

   The existing `preference-options-routes.integration.test.ts` loop over the list then covers it. `#36071` does not touch `service-messaging`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36074-comment-reply-notice.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-audit': patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset body. That is right for what the diff publishes:
- the new topic and message keys are a non-protocol widening;
- no key, value or metadata type that an author can write is added, narrowed or changed in meaning;
- under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, a non-protocol widening ships `patch`;
- no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.

The amendment 7063394639 moved the claim's `Clause-②: no` to `yes (widening)` on the final diff. I agree with it.

The fix in ① 7 adds a second package to the changeset, `'@objectstack/service-messaging': patch`. It is the same kind of change (a value added to a served suggestion list) and keeps the same declarations.

Clause-②: yes (widening). Confirmed for the head as reviewed. It stays `yes (widening)` once ① 7 lands.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: item 3's "which record" in the title. Answered: accept.** The title names the actor only, as "X mentioned you" does. The notice's `source` is the record and opens `/{object}/{id}`. Naming the record would need a per-recipient read of the title field. The card lists item 3 under 协调席自己加的, so it was not the maintainer's words. The claim stated this reading before the build, and the PR body states it again. No escalation is needed. If the coordinator wants the record name, that is a follow-up card.
- **Dev flag: e-mail rate "沿用现有的". Answered: accept.** The reply e-mail uses the mention window (10 min, per organization and person) under its own key, so the card's acceptance holds: three replies in one window send one e-mail. A side effect is that one mention e-mail and one reply e-mail can both arrive in the same window. That is disclosed in the PR body and changeset, and it never holds back a mention. A reply that mentions the recipient sends only the mention, so the case the card names is never doubled.
- **Dev flag: "participants" = starter plus everyone up the chain plus distinct authors of direct replies to the root. Answered: accept, with a nit.** For a reply to a reply, the authors of other nested replies under intermediate comments are not found, because only the root's direct children are grouped. The Console writes one level, so today this is unreachable. Nit, no change required.
- **Card acceptance.** Each line is covered by the new integration cases:
  - the starter is notified and the replier is not;
  - in an A, B, C chain, A and B are notified and C is not;
  - a mention suppresses the reply notice;
  - a starter who lost read access gets nothing;
  - three replies in one window send one e-mail;
  - the PR body says how participants are found.
- **open_questions.** The card has none beyond its 没有核对的 section. Landing the click on the reply itself depends on 评论（一）, and this card asks only for opening the record, which is met.
- **SQL push-down.**
  - The participant read is ONE grouped `engine.aggregate` (`WHERE parent_id = ? GROUP BY author_id`, on the existing `parent_id` index). The thread's rows are never materialised. This is pushed down.
  - The ancestry walk is one `find` per hop, bounded at 16 and cycle-safe. Reason given: the Console writes one level, so this is one read, and the engine offers no recursive query. Accepted.
  - The per-candidate gate is the existing `admitMentionRecipients`, reused. It is per-envelope by necessity, because each recipient is judged under their own grants. It adds no new id materialisation or in-app join. Accepted.
  - No finding.
- **Nit (no effect):** in `writeCommentReplyNotices`, `if (uid === actorId) continue;` is redundant, because the candidates already exclude the actor and the gate drops the actor too.

## 维护者速读
这一轮有两处改动，都可以通过：
- **上一轮我提的建议已经做了。** 找「这一串的人」时，现在只认同一条记录上的评论。万一有一条回复挂到了别的记录的评论下面，不会去通知那边的人。新加了一条测试钉住这一点。
- **座位 L2 要求的补充也做了。** 通知设置和模板的话题列表里，现在会列出「评论回复」。即使这个组织还没收到过回复通知，管理员也能直接在设置里关掉回复邮件。

另外删掉了一处重复的判断，不影响结果。不属于受管面，按普通队列落地。CI 绿了再落地；L2 这一轮是否要复核由座位定。

**Head reviewed:** `920db11e64204a453a7ed6d479ced57caaa4d506`. The delta is `c83ad1dc..920db11e`, two commits (`6c5503f0`, `920db11e`), 4 files, +36/−12. `git merge-tree` onto current `main` is clean. `check-governed-merges --pr 36098` reads **NOT governed**, 0 of 12 paths. `reviewFace` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` still gives `declaration` → `TIER_DEFAULT`. The prior ACCEPT 7063795484 stands for everything outside this delta.

### N1: cleared (`6c5503f0`)
- `readThreadParticipants` now takes the reply's `thread_id` and returns `null` when it is empty. Each hop reads `thread_id` and stops when it differs, so a parent on another record yields no root and no notice at all.
- The grouped read's `where` is `{ parent_id: rootId, thread_id: threadId }`, so sibling replies are held to the same record too.
- The new case writes a reply on `t1` whose `parent_id` names a comment on `t2`. It asserts that no `collab.reply` delivery and no send come from it, and the thread reports that it fails with the bound removed.

### `920db11e` (seat L2 7063833407 item ①7)
- `collab.reply` joins `PLATFORM_NOTIFICATION_TOPICS` in sorted position, after `collab.mention`. That satisfies the route test's sorted-order assertion and its every-platform-topic-offered loop (`preference-options-routes.integration.test.ts:205-208`). The doc line names the send site.
- The changeset adds `@objectstack/service-messaging: patch`, and its Clause-② line names the list widening. The new value in an exported list and in the `preference-options` answer is a widening, so `yes (widening)` still holds.
- The removed `if (uid === actorId) continue;` was redundant. Candidates drop the actor before the gate, and the gate only admits ids it was given (each raw id resolves to itself), so the actor cannot come back.

### N2
- It is stated in the body as a known cost, as asked. Nothing more is needed here.

### Landing terms
- Not governed: the seat lands it through the ordinary queue on this head's green. `Fixes #36074` closes the card on merge. Whether the declaration L2 needs a delta read for `920db11e` is the seat's call; this record does not replace it.
- At the time of this record CI on `920db11e` is still running, per the card thread.
- A new push needs a delta L1 unless it is a clean main merge.
- This review does not approve, mark ready, enqueue or request review.
